That single collision is a reminder that even a quiet stretch of US-101 SB, the intersection near 11715 Blue Slide Road, the SR-283 Eagle Prairie Bridge, or the section of US-101 near Davis Street can turn into the site of a life-changing injury. Reports also show that crashes here tend to cluster on Saturday afternoons, between roughly 3 and 5 p.m., which may reflect weekend traffic patterns. There's no obligation to move forward, and if you do, we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover money.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Clock Runs Out

items.title: California Gives You Two Years — Usually
items.desc: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the crash. If a government vehicle or agency was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it pays to check early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, which means even if you share some blame for the collision, you can still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases, so the full impact of your injury can be considered.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning our fee comes only from money recovered on your behalf — never out of your pocket up front.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Rio Dell?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering damages. Your compensation would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, which we can help assess.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Rio Dell?
items.answer: Public collision records point to a handful of corridors with higher reported counts, including US-101 SB, the area near 11715 Blue Slide Road, the SR-283 Eagle Prairie Bridge, and US-101 near Davis Street. These are simply where reported crashes have clustered — not a judgment on any specific road.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in standard personal injury cases, which means the full scope of your experience can be factored into a claim.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for a free case review. If you choose to move forward, we work on contingency, so you don't pay unless we recover money for you.
